title: Rhubarb and Orange Icebox Cake
changes_from_base: Home-baked butter biscuits sandwiched with a rhubarb-orange filling and covered in whipped cream, set in the fridge, instead of sponge and ice cream.
summary: Stacks of light vanilla biscuits are sandwiched with a tangy orange-scented rhubarb filling, then coated in softly whipped cream for a pretty, fridge-set dessert.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
caster sugar, plus a little for pressing

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Grease or line 2 baking trays. Stir together the 1 tbsp vanilla, 1½ tsp baking powder and ¾ tsp fine salt, then beat with the 149 g caster sugar and 227 g soft butter until smooth, mixing in the 240 g plain flour until a dryish dough comes together.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Scoop 1 tsp portions of dough spaced 4 cm apart on the lined trays and flatten each to 6 mm using the base of a sugared glass.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake at 150 °C for 20-25 min until very light golden, then cool completely on a rack.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Simmer the 482 g rhubarb with 100 g caster sugar, the nutmeg and 14 g orange zest for 15-20 min until some liquid cooks off, then stir in the cornflour mixed with 49 g sugar and 2 tbsp cold water and boil until thick and no longer cloudy, and cool completely.

steps.title: Whip
steps.text: Whip the 454 g double cream with 1 tbsp caster sugar until tracks show, then add 2 tsp vanilla and whip to a stiff, smooth cream.

steps.title: Sandwich
steps.text: Sandwich stacks of 4 biscuits with 1 tbsp rhubarb filling between each layer.

steps.title: Assemble
steps.text: Lay the stacks on their sides in a row or ring on a plate and cover every surface with the whipped cream.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Chill for at least 4 h or overnight, garnishing with strawberries if using.

tips: Cool the rhubarb filling fully before assembling so the cream stays firm.
Whip the cream just to stiff peaks; overwhipping will make it grainy.
Arrange the biscuit stacks close together before coating so the cream covers every gap.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keeps in the fridge for up to 1 week with the cut sides covered.
